audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Kennen, Kennen, Kennen, Kennen, Skill, Kennen, Kennen. Level 1 was marked Kennen under a why that opens 'Level 1 is even'; Level 6 was marked Skill under a why that ends 'you win this duel outright'; 2+ items was marked Kennen under a why warning you not to get caught by his ult.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill, Kennen, Kennen, Kennen, Kennen, Kennen, Skill on 674 games at 53.26%, and it matches the prose already written under each row.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Skill, row 4 to Kennen, row 6 to Skill, as matched pairs in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ult asymmetry — the thing the whole page tells you to track — is never quantified.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s; Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s that never shortens. At rank 1 you get your ult back first; by his rank 3 he does. That inversion is the entire 'when do I fight' answer and it was missing.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) 'his Ground Slam shield' appears in whys[2], mid and wants.foe[1] — Ground Slam is not a shield. It is a 7-second shockwave dealing magic damage based on his Armor and cutting your Attack Speed. The shield is Granite Shield, his passive. (b) tldr, report[0], report[1], dosFull[2] and wants.you[2] tell you to 'E-dash' his R; Lightning Rush is a morph with Move Speed, not a dash.
audit.why: The Ground Slam attack-speed cut is the highest-value line in this matchup and it was entirely absent: Kennen's stun is a three-mark counter and Electrical Surge supplies marks ON HIT, so slowing his attack speed pushes the third mark — and the stun — later. Meanwhile Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max Health and RECHARGES if he is not hit for a few seconds, which is what actually rewards continuous poke over burst.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam restated as the attack-speed throttle on your mark supply in phases[3].why and whys[3]; the shield re-attributed to Granite Shield with the recharge condition in whys[2], mid, wants.foe[1] and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The _missing feed proposes 'Malphite bypasses stacking resistances (Granite Shield)'. I did not write it.
audit.why: The percentHealth flag on Granite Shield describes the SHIELD being 10% of his own maximum Health. It is not percent-health damage against you, so there is nothing here that invalidates your resistances.
audit.corrected: No resistance-bypass line written. What I did write is the recharge condition, which is the part that actually changes play.

edits.before: This is your lane to take. By levels 4-5 your Q poke has him low and his Ground Slam shield can't out-sustain magic chip. At 6 you own the window outright: Q-W to pre-stack marks, E (Lightning Rush) in for the third-stack stun, then Slicing Maelstrom rips through his armor for the kill — his W shield and stacked armor are worthless against it. The only thing to respect is his Unstoppable Force (R): bait it or save Flash/E to dodge, because his sole kill path is flash-engaging it into a jungle gank.
edits.after: This is your lane to take. By levels 4-5 continuous Q chip keeps Granite Shield from ever recharging, so his effective HP never resets. At 6 you own the window outright: Q-W to pre-stack marks, E (Lightning Rush) in for the third-stack stun, then Slicing Maelstrom on a flat 120s for the kill — stacked armour does nothing to magic. Respect two things only: Ground Slam every 7 seconds, whose attack-speed cut delays your Surge marks, and a 130-second Unstoppable Force flash-engaged into a jungle gank.

notes: Mirror (malphite__kennen) already made the Ground Slam / Electrical Surge finding; this file states the same fact from Kennen's side, so the two directions agree. One thing neither side asserts, per the mirror's own note: whether Seismic Shard or Ground Slam's grounding can deny Lightning Rush. Riot calls Lightning Rush a morph that lets him pass through units, not a dash, so grounding should be irrelevant — but the kits do not say it outright and I will not assert it. Also unaddressed: dosFull[2].t 'E-dash out of his R' is 19 characters, under the applier's 25-character skip threshold, so the E-dash phrasing survives there and in report[0]/report[1]; worth a manual pass.
